home-no-project-recovery.scope: PINNED FURTHER by a three-point alignment experiment on an ext4 worktree (the environment the Owner specified), the first run of this defect that ever reached an assertion cleanly. The break is now localised to the router's location-signal sync, NOT to the picker, the draft creation, or the navigate call. Interleaved evidence from one pass, all timestamps in order: `newDraft` ENTERED with draftID and href `/new-session?draftId=…`; its `setStore` ran and the IN-MEMORY store already contained the new draft (`storeDrafts=[…] containsNew=true` — so the lookup at `packages/app/src/app.tsx:351` would have found it, had `DraftRoute` been reached, which it was not, so `[DIAG store]` never printed); `about to call navigate`; the router RECEIVED it (`router navigate RECEIVED href=/new-session?draftId=…`) and returned; `navigate returned`; THEN `Routes RENDER url=/ enteredNewSession=false`; the router's location signal was still `/`; only afterwards did `history.pushState url=/new-session?…` and a `history.replaceState url=undefined` hit the browser; the browser URL did become the draft URL; and no event follows. So: the app's own store, the navigate call and the history commit all did what they should, and the router's location signal did not advance. Decisive branch from the decision tree: `navigate` called AND received by the router, but `Routes` re-rendered for `/` only — the router location-signal sync, with the `replaceState(undefined)` immediately after `pushState` as the prime suspect. ENVIRONMENT NOTE: the same spec on the FUSE checkout stalls inside `expectDevServerReady` on most attempts; on an ext4 worktree with `rsync -aH` copied deps (the `-H` matters — Bun's `.nfs`/`.bun` store is hardlinked, plain `-a` duplicates ~8GB) and a private port it reached an assertion on the first try. UPDATE, same day: that `replaceState(undefined)` prime suspect has since been CLEARED by the router-internal experiment recorded in `unlock` below — read it there before treating this paragraph as the current state.
home-no-project-recovery.unlock: ROUTER-INTERNAL EXPERIMENT DONE (the Owner-approved option A), and it answered both questions the Owner asked. Run as a focused reproduction against the REAL `@solidjs/router` 0.15.4 + `solid-js` 1.9.10 under happy-dom, because the browser-level instrument is environmentally blocked here: with the dev server up, `GET /` did not answer in 600s while the vite process sat in `request_wait_answer` and the FUSE backing device held ~98% utilisation, and a two-test unit run costs ~40s of pure I/O. Eleven variants in one run, each logging the router's own location, the rendered surface and every history write in order. TWO RESULTS, quoted from that run. (a) The trailing `history.replaceState url=undefined` is ROUTER-INTERNAL AND BENIGN: it is emitted by EVERY variant including all the ones that work (V1 sync navigate, V2 from `Promise.then`, V3 inside `startTransition`, V4 the exact store-write-then-navigate shape, V6 two navigations in one microtask), and it is `saveCurrentDepth()` at `node_modules/@solidjs/router/dist/lifecycle.js:36-41` writing `_depth` into the history state. It is NOT the app's `clearAuthToken` (`packages/app/src/entry.tsx:119`, which only runs when an `auth_token` param is present) and it does not reset the signal. So the prime suspect recorded in the previous round is cleared. (b) A route component that THROWS while the transition commits reproduces the signature: `router location` logs `/blank` and is never logged again, `history.pushState url=/new-session?draftId=d7` still happens, and the rendered surface stays absent (`surface=undefined fellBackHome=false`) — the commit is aborted, the location signal keeps its old value, and the browser URL advances anyway. ALSO RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, not by reasoning: the picker-callback shape is not the cause, since navigating from inside `Promise.then` (V2) and from inside `startTransition` (V3) both commit and render normally; and `useBeforeLeave` + `preventDefault` (V8, the `DirtyDraftGuard` shape at `context/chat-workspace.tsx:168-181`) does not match either, because the navigation then never reaches the browser at all (no `pushState`) whereas the app's URL does change. A `<Suspense>`-wrapped lazy route whose promise never settles (V11, the shape of `lazy(() => import("@/pages/new-session"))` at `app.tsx:80` under the route Suspense at `pages/layout.tsx:99`) advances the router's location but renders nothing, so a Suspense hold is a live second candidate. A THIRD candidate was tested and RULED OUT: the app's own `DraftRoute` shape — the `tabs.ready()` gate plus the `keyed` store lookup whose fallback is `fallback={<Navigate href="/" />}` (`app.tsx:345-359`) — was driven in all three orderings that could matter (the draft row and `ready()` both true before the route renders; both flipping true together with the store write after the route is mounted; `ready()` already true while the store row arrives with the navigate). All three commit and render the draft surface, and the `Navigate` fallback never fires (`fellBackHome=false` in every one), so a late store row or a closed ready-gate is not the trigger either. The candidate list is now exactly two: a throw during the commit, or a Suspense hold. RELEVANT PRE-EXISTING MARKER: the comment at `pages/layout.tsx:84-98` already names this exact defect as the single untested trigger of that route Suspense. STILL UNVERIFIED, stated as a hypothesis only: which of the two candidates (a throw during the commit, or a Suspense hold) is the app's actual cause. The throw candidate fits 'the location signal did not advance AND the browser URL did'; the Suspense candidate fits 'the lazy module was never even requested'. They are distinguished by one observation the instrument added for this step already prints. BLOCKED on running the instrumented reproduction ONCE in a browser on a healthy host, and nothing else — no further localisation is needed. NOTE ON THE INSTRUMENT: the diagnostic scaffolding was applied to `packages/app/src/app.tsx`, `packages/app/src/context/tabs.tsx` and a scratch spec to take the measurements above, and has been REMOVED before this record was committed, so it does not sit in the tree. Re-creating it is mechanical and its exact contents are specified here: gate a `diag(label, detail)` helper on `window.__DIAG__ === true` so a normal run logs nothing; log `DIAG DraftRoute entered` plus the `tabs.store.find(...)` result at `app.tsx:351`; log the router's own location by reading `useLocation()` in a `null`-rendering child of the router root (reading it inside `Routes` would add a location subscriber and could change the outcome being measured) together with `window.location` in `Routes`; log in `tabs.newDraft` (`context/tabs.tsx:167`) the draftID, href and the store contents after `setStore`; and in the spec set `__DIAG__` from an init script and wrap `history.pushState`/`history.replaceState` to print url, state and a stack. It must run on an ext4 worktree with `rsync -aH` copied deps and a private port, with no sleep/retry/reload/repeated-clicking/relaxed assertions. Read it for: whether `DIAG DraftRoute entered` fires (it not firing points at the Suspense hold; an exception before it points at the throw), and whether any `pageerror`/`console` error is present. IF EITHER CANDIDATE IS CONFIRMED, the fix unit's minimum deliverable is: make the committed red reproduction pass, prove the first picker pass actually mounts the draft, keep zero early `POST /session`, add a control case for a NONEXISTENT draftId (which must still fall back per contract), and show the legal/illegal draft behaviours differ, followed by targeted typecheck/lint/prettier/diff-check and an E2E tally. If the instrumented run instead reaches an assertion with neither candidate confirmed, report insufficient evidence and request a widened scope rather than editing candidates.
